docs.title: qccompute
docs.text: Runs quantum chemistry programs on qcdata inputs using qccodec codecs and returns structured results. Built-in support for TeraChem, ORCA, Psi4, CREST, xtb, and geomeTRIC, and any program you define a qccodec.Codec for.

docs.title: The QC Suite
docs.text:
These packages work together to make quantum chemistry fast, structured, and interoperable.

  • qcref - Reference data for computational chemistry: CODATA physical constants, conversion factors, a periodic table, and solvent properties, each value with its source.
  • qcdata - Data structures for quantum chemistry inputs and results, with Jupyter visualizations. Documentation
  • qcinf - Cheminformatics algorithms and structure utilities for qcdata structures.
  • qccodec - Translates qcdata inputs into native program inputs and parses program outputs back into qcdata objects, one codec per program. Documentation
  • qccompute - Runs quantum chemistry programs on qcdata inputs using qccodec codecs and returns structured results. Documentation
  • BigChem - Distributed execution of qccompute calculations across clusters of computers or the cloud.
  • ChemCloud - A web application and Python client that expose a BigChem cluster securely over the internet.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: python -m pip install qccompute

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Complete, runnable scripts for every supported program and calculation type, with every common option shown and each program's quirks explained, are on the qccodec program pages.

qccompute uses the qcdata data structures to drive quantum chemistry programs in a standardized way. This allows for a simple and consistent interface to a wide variety of quantum chemistry programs. See the qcdata library for documentation on the input and output data structures.

The compute function is the main entry point for the library and is used to run a calculation.

from qcdata import Structure, ProgramInput
from qccompute import compute
from qccompute.exceptions import ExternalProgramError

# Create the Structure
h2o = Structure.open("h2o.xyz")

# Define the program input
prog_input = ProgramInput(
    program="terachem",
    structure=h2o,
    calctype="energy",
    model={"method": "wb97xd3", "basis": "def2-svp"},
    keywords={"purify": "no", "restricted": False},
)

# Run the calculation; will return a ProgramOutput or raise an exception
try:
    prog_output = compute(prog_input, collect_files=True)
except ExternalProgramError as e:
    # External QQ program failed in some way
    prog_output = e.prog_output
    prog_output.input_data # Input data used by the QC program
    prog_output.success # Will be False
    prog_output.results # Any half-computed results before the failure
    prog_output.logs # Logs from the calculation
    prog_output.plogs # Shortcut to print out the logs in human readable format
    prog_output.traceback # Stack trace from the calculation
    prog_output.ptraceback # Shortcut to print out the traceback in human readable format
    raise e
else:
    # Calculation succeeded
    prog_output.input_data # Input data used by the QC program
    prog_output.success # Will be True
    prog_output.results # All structured data and files from the calculation
    prog_output.results.files # Any files returned by the calculation
    prog_output.logs # Logs from the calculation
    prog_output.plogs # Shortcut to print out the logs in human readable format
    prog_output.results.provenance # Provenance information about the calculation
    prog_output.extras # Any extra information not in the schema

One may also call compute(..., raise_exc=False) to return a ProgramOutput object rather than raising an exception when a calculation fails. This may allow easier handling of failures in some cases.

from qcdata import Structure, ProgramInput
from qccompute import compute
from qccompute.exceptions import ExternalProgramError
# Create the Structure
h2o = Structure.open("h2o.xyz")

# Define the program input
prog_input = ProgramInput(
    program="terachem",
    structure=h2o,
    calctype="energy",
    model={"method": "wb97xd3", "basis": "def2-svp"},
    keywords={"purify": "no", "restricted": False},
)

# Run the calculation; will return a ProgramOutput object
prog_output = compute(prog_input, collect_files=True, raise_exc=False)
if not prog_output.success:
    # Same as except block above

else:
    # Same as else block above

Alternatively, the compute_args function can be used to run a calculation with the input data structures passed in as arguments rather than as a single ProgramInput object.

from qcdata import Structure
from qccompute import compute_args
# Create the Structure
h2o = Structure.open("h2o.xyz")

# Run the calculation
prog_output = compute_args(
    "terachem",
    h2o,
    calctype="energy",
    model={"method": "wb97xd3", "basis": "def2-svp"},
    keywords={"purify": "no", "restricted": False},
    files={...},
    collect_files=True
)

The behavior of compute() and compute_args() can be tuned by passing in keyword arguments like collect_files shown above. Arguments can modify which scratch directory location to use, whether to delete or keep the scratch files after a calculation completes, what files to collect from a calculation, whether to stream the program logs in real time as the program executes, and whether to propagate a wavefunction through a series of calculations. Arguments also include hooks for passing in update functions that can be called as a program executes in real time. See the qccompute.compute docstring for details.

See the /examples directory for more examples.

docs.title: ✨ Visualization ✨
docs.text:
Visualize all your results with a single line of code!

First install the visualization module:

python -m pip install qcdata[view]

or if your shell requires '' around arguments with brackets:

python -m pip install 'qcdata[view]'

Then in a Jupyter notebook import the qcdata view module and call view.view(...) passing it one or any number of qcdata objects you want to visualize, including Structure objects or any ProgramOutput object. You may also pass arrays of titles and/or subtitles to add additional information to the molecular structure display. If no titles are passed, qcdata will look for Structure identifiers such as a name or SMILES to label the Structure.

Seamless visualizations for ProgramOutput objects make results analysis easy!

Single point calculations display their results in a table.

If you want to use the HTML generated by the viewer to build your own dashboards, use the functions inside qcdata.view.py that begin with generate_ to create HTML you can insert into any dashboard.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: If you have any issues with qccompute or would like to request a feature, please open an issue.

docs.title: Custom programs
docs.text:
qccompute only executes; everything program-specific comes from a qccodec Codec. When a program is not built in, define one in your script and pass it to compute, or register it so it is found by name (including as a geomeTRIC gradient child):

from qcdata import CalcType, ProgramInput
from qccodec import Codec, SubprocessInput, re_search
import qccodec, qccompute

codec = Codec("myprog", calctypes={CalcType.energy})

@codec.encoder
def encode(inp: ProgramInput) -> SubprocessInput:
    return SubprocessInput(("myprog", "run.inp"), files={"run.inp": inp.require_structure().to_xyz()})

@codec.parser(target="energy", calctypes=[CalcType.energy])
def parse_energy(stdout: str) -> float:
    return float(re_search(r"Total energy:\s+(-?\d+\.\d+)", stdout).group(1))

output = qccompute.compute(prog_input, codec=codec)   # explicit
qccodec.register(codec)
output = qccompute.compute(prog_input)                # by program name

Program-specific decode options are passed with options=; each codec declares the options it accepts in codec.options and unknown names are rejected:

compute(prog_input, options={"collect_rotamers": True})   # CREST

docs.title: Development
docs.text: See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup, the pre-commit workflow, running tests, and the release process.

docs.title: How a calculation runs
docs.text:
1. compute() resolves a codec: the codec= argument, a codec registered with qccodec.register, a built-in, or one installed by another package.
  2. codec.encode(input_data) returns a SubprocessInput (command + files) or a PythonInput (callable + arguments). Encoding never executes anything.
  3. qccompute creates the scratch directory, stages the files, and runs run_subprocess or run_python. Both merge stdout and stderr into one log; Python capture includes native writes to the stdout/stderr file descriptors and the loggers the codec names.
  4. codec.decode(input_data, native_output) is always called, even after an execution failure, so partial results are recovered. Exceptions carrying .data keep it.
  5. Requested files and wavefunctions are collected, the directory is removed if rm_scratch_dir is True, and the ProgramOutput is built. On failure, the exception's .prog_output holds the complete failed output.

Environment: invocation defaults from the codec override inherited values, and environment= overrides both. Subprocess overrides are local to the child. Python execution temporarily changes the process environment, working directory, and output streams under a reentrant lock, so use separate processes for independent concurrent Python calculations. xtb and CREST default to OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 in their child environments.

Executables: a program runs from the first of compute(..., executables={"orca": "/opt/orca/orca"}), the environment variable QCCOMPUTE_<PROGRAM>_EXECUTABLE (for example QCCOMPUTE_ORCA_EXECUTABLE), or the codec's command found on PATH. Use this when the program is not on PATH, or when another program shadows its name, such as the GNOME screen reader named orca. Child calculations use the same mapping. The program always runs by its absolute path, which ORCA requires for parallel runs, and that path is recorded in output.execution.extras["executable"].

Timeouts: compute(..., timeout=3600) kills any program that runs longer, together with every process it started, and raises ProgramTimeoutError with partial results attached. The limit applies to each program run, including geomeTRIC's child gradients; Python callables themselves are not interrupted.

Logs: subprocess callbacks stream (all_logs, new_logs) with a final callback for remaining output; update_interval is a minimum spacing. Python callbacks receive the captured log once after invocation. Logs remain attached on failure even with collect_logs=False.

Child calculations: geomeTRIC drives gradients through an injected callback, with a separate workspace and ProgramOutput for each child. Child codecs are resolved by program name. propagate_wfn=True keeps each child's wavefunction files and calls the child codec's propagate_wfn(output, input_data) so the next step starts from them.

Exceptions: CodecNotFoundError, InputError, ProgramNotFoundError, and ExternalProgramError all derive from QCComputeBaseError and carry .prog_output. The older AdapterNotFoundError/AdapterInputError names remain as aliases for one release.

docs.title: TeraChem FE/PBS dependency
docs.text: The optional FE/PBS codecs require a separate tcpb migration. Published tcpb==0.16.0 constructs the old qcdata models internally, so requests report an explicit dependency error (or return a failed ProgramOutput when raise_exc=False). Standard TeraChem subprocess execution is independent of this limitation.

docs.title: Custom codec
docs.text:
Run a program qccodec doesn't support by defining its codec in your own script. The codec turns a ProgramInput into the program's command and files, and parses the output back into qcdata. Pass it as codec=, or register it to use the program by name, including as a geomeTRIC gradient child. qccodec's Writing a codec guide covers parsers, failure detection, and testing.

"""Define a codec for a program qccodec does not know about, and run it.

The "program" here is a Python one-liner so the example runs anywhere; swap the
command and regex for the real thing.
"""

import sys

import qccodec
from qccodec import Codec, SubprocessInput, re_search
from qcdata import CalcType, ProgramInput, SinglePointData, Structure

from qccompute import compute

codec = Codec("myprog", calctypes={CalcType.energy})


@codec.encoder
def encode(inp: ProgramInput) -> SubprocessInput:
    """Write the program's input file and build its command line."""
    assert inp.model is not None
    run_inp = f"method {inp.model.method}\n{inp.require_structure().to_xyz()}"
    # Stand-in for ("myprog", "run.inp")
    command = (sys.executable, "-c", "print('Total energy: -1.5')")
    return SubprocessInput(command, files={"run.inp": run_inp})


@codec.parser(target="energy", calctypes=[CalcType.energy])
def parse_energy(stdout: str) -> float:
    """Pull the final energy out of the program's stdout."""
    return float(re_search(r"Total energy:\s+(-?\d+\.\d+)", stdout).group(1))


@codec.parser(target=("provenance", "program_version"), required=False)
def parse_version(stdout: str) -> str:
    """Record the version when the program prints one."""
    return re_search(r"myprog version (\S+)", stdout).group(1)


prog_input = ProgramInput(
    program="myprog",
    calctype="energy",  # type: ignore
    structure=Structure(symbols=["H", "H"], geometry=[[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1.4]]),  # type: ignore
    model={"method": "wb97x-d"},  # type: ignore
)

# Pass the codec explicitly...
output = compute(prog_input, codec=codec)
assert isinstance(output.results, SinglePointData)
print("energy:", output.results.energy)

# ...or register it once and run by program name, e.g. as a geomeTRIC gradient child.
qccodec.register(codec)
output = compute(prog_input)
print("provenance:", output.results.provenance)

docs.title: File Input
docs.text:
The File Input can be used as an escape hatch when you want to perform a calculation type that is not yet supported by qccompute or use a program not yet supported by qccompute. You can submit the program's native input files to the program and qccompute will execute the program, collect all the outputs, and return them to you. These calculations could be an MD run, some unique calculation type not supported by qccompute, or any arbitrary command you can send to any command-line executable program.

"""An example of how to create a FileInput object for a QC Program."""

from pathlib import Path

from qcdata import FileInput, Structure

from qccompute import compute

# Input files for QC Program
inp_file = Path("path/to/tc.in").read_text()  # Or your own function to create tc.in

# Structure object to XYZ file
structure = Structure.open("path/to/my/mol.xyz")
xyz_str = structure.to_xyz()  # type: ignore

# Create a FileInput object for TeraChem
file_input = FileInput(
    program="terachem",
    files={"tc.in": inp_file, "coords.xyz": xyz_str},
    cmdline_args=["tc.in"],
)

# This will write the files to disk in a temporary directory and then run
# "terachem tc.in" in that directory.
prog_output = compute(file_input, print_logs=True)

# Data
print(prog_output.logs)
print(prog_output.input_data)
print(prog_output.results.files)  # Has all the files terachem creates
print(prog_output.results.files.keys())  # File names
# Saves all outputs with the exact structure produced by the QC program
prog_output.results.save_files("to/this/directory")

docs.title: Many calculations at once
docs.text:
compute takes a single input or a list of them. A list returns a list of outputs in input order, and every other argument applies to each input.

from qccompute import compute

outputs = compute([inp1, inp2, inp3])

docs.title: What runs in parallel
docs.text:
• Programs (ORCA, xtb, Psi4, TeraChem, DFTB+, CREST, ...) run side by side. Each runs in its own directory with its own captured output, exactly as a single calculation does.
  • Python calculations (machine-learned potentials, tblite, geomeTRIC) take over a process's output streams, working directory, and environment while they run. When a list holds two or more, they run side by side in worker processes: qccompute starts them with python -m qccompute._worker, so your script is never re-run and needs no if __name__ == "__main__": guard. A worker starts with OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, and MKL_NUM_THREADS set to its share of the cores (unless you set them), so the workers' numerical libraries do not each start a thread per core. A worker that needs a GPU is started on its own device.
  • Machine-learned potentials (AIMNet2, TorchANI, MACE, Orb, FAIR-Chem) evaluate many structures in one pass. Inputs their codec can batch run together in this process; see Batches.
  • Python calculations whose codec exists only in your process and cannot be pickled (for example one built with lambdas and registered with qccodec.register), single Python inputs, and lists computed inside a calculation run in this process, one at a time.

docs.title: Cores and GPUs
docs.text:
max_workers is a budget of CPU threads: by default, the cores this process may use. Each calculation draws the threads its codec declares from what the input asks for (ORCA's pal, Psi4's -n, CREST's threads, xtb's parallel), and one otherwise. So pal 8 ORCA runs on a 32-core machine run four at a time, with no extra setting. Calculations start in input order; one that asks for more threads than the budget runs alone.

GPU programs (TeraChem) get their own devices: each calculation runs with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set to its GPUs, as many at once as there are GPUs. The GPUs are those in CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES if it is set (in environment or the process), or else those nvidia-smi lists. If none are found, GPU calculations run one at a time without pinning.

docs.title: Batches
docs.text:
A codec that can batch (Codec(encode_batch=..., batch_key=...), qccodec 0.19.0) says which inputs may share a pass: for the machine-learned potentials, energy and gradient inputs with the same program, model, and keywords. Such inputs in a list are evaluated in batches of up to codec.max_batch (32 by default), each one call of the model, and each value is decoded as if its input had run alone.

from qcdata import ProgramInput

inputs = [
    ProgramInput(
        structure=s, calctype="gradient", model={"method": "aimnet2"}, program="aimnet2"
    )
    for s in structures
]
outputs = compute(inputs)  # one model call for up to 32 structures

On a laptop GPU (RTX 3050 Ti), 40 water gradients took 0.41 s one at a time and 0.05 s as a list with AIMNet2, 0.58 s and 0.04 s with TorchANI, and 1.22 s and 0.24 s with MACE.

  • Batches run in this process, after the programs of the list, so a loaded model stays cached for the next compute call, as in iterative methods such as NEB.
  • Each output's execution.extras records batch_size and batch_index; its wall_time and logs are the batch's.
  • A batch that runs out of GPU memory is split in half until it fits. A batch that fails otherwise is computed again one input at a time, so each failure is reported with its own input. A value that fails to decode fails only its input.
  • Hessians, inputs whose key is unique, and lists with collect_files or collect_wfn (a batch shares one directory) run as usual.
  • Results match single calculations to the model's precision; models computing in float32 or TF32 on a GPU (Orb's default float32-high) differ in the last digits.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
Every calculation runs first. Then, with raise_exc=True (the default), one ComputeErrors is raised if any failed. It is an ExceptionGroup: each sub-exception is the error that calculation would have raised on its own, with its prog_output and its position in the list as input_index, and outputs holds every output.

from qccompute.exceptions import ComputeErrors, ProgramTimeoutError

try:
    outputs = compute(inputs, timeout=600)
except* ProgramTimeoutError as timeouts:
    print(f"{len(timeouts.exceptions)} calculations timed out")

With raise_exc=False the list is returned as is; check each output.success.

Four geomeTRIC optimizations of a six-water cluster with xtb gradients (117 steps each) took 49.7 s one after another and 7.3 s in four workers on a 16-core laptop. Much of that is the thread limit: numpy's BLAS starts a thread per core by default, which slows geomeTRIC's small matrices even in a single process, where OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 alone brought the four optimizations from 49.7 s to 18.5 s.

docs.title: Following progress
docs.text: print_logs=True prints every line of output prefixed with its input's index, such as [3]. An update_func receives (index, all_logs, new_logs) and is called from the threads running the calculations, so it must be thread-safe.

docs.title: Interrupting
docs.text: Ctrl-C stops the list: queued calculations are dropped and running programs are killed together with every process they started.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Calculations are run by calling the qccompute.compute() function with the relevant arguments and keywords like this:

from qcdata import Structure, ProgramInput
from qccompute import compute

# Create the Structure
structure = Structure(
    symbols=["O", "H", "H"],
    geometry=[  # type: ignore
        [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
        [0.52421003, 1.68733646, 0.48074633],
        [1.14668581, -0.45032174, -1.35474466],
    ],
)

# Define the program input
prog_input = ProgramInput(
    program="terachem",
    structure=structure,
    calctype="energy",
    model={"method": "wb97xd3", "basis": "def2-svp"},
    keywords={"purify": "no", "restricted": False},
)

# Run the calculation; will return a ProgramOutput or raise an exception
result = compute(prog_input, collect_files=True)

The compute function resolves a codec and executes its native invocation. It also accepts an explicit local codec=. The available arguments are:

docs.title: qccompute.main.compute(input_data: InputType | Sequence[InputType], *, codec: qccodec.Codec | None = None, environment: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, scratch_dir: StrOrPath | None = None, rm_scratch_dir: bool = True, collect_logs: bool = True, collect_files: bool = False, collect_wfn: bool = False, update_func: Callable[..., None] | None = None, update_interval: float | None = None, print_logs: bool = False, raise_exc: bool = True, propagate_wfn: bool = False, options: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, timeout: float | None = None, executables: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, max_workers: int | None = None) -> ProgramOutput[InputType, Data] | list[ProgramOutput[InputType, Data]]
docs.text:
Compute one input, or a list of inputs in parallel, with a local runner.

A single input returns a single ProgramOutput. A list (or tuple) returns a list of outputs in input order; its inputs may be for different programs, and every other argument applies to each of them. Calculations that run as programs (ORCA, xtb, Psi4, ...) run side by side in threads. Calculations that run in Python (geomeTRIC, tblite) take over a process's output streams while they run, so two or more of them run side by side in worker processes, which start with the numerical libraries' thread counts set to their share. All of them draw on the max_workers budget. Inputs a codec can evaluate together (machine-learned potentials sharing a model) run in batches in this process, one call per batch of up to codec.max_batch; execution.extras records batch_size and batch_index.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default input_data InputType | Sequence[InputType]

A qcdata input object, such as ProgramInput or FileInput, or a list of them.

required codec Codec | None

The qccodec.Codec translating this program's inputs and outputs. If None, resolve one with qccodec.get_codec(input_data): a codec registered with qccodec.register, a built-in, or one installed by another package.

None environment Mapping[str, str] | None

Process environment overrides mapping strings to strings. Applied after the inherited environment and codec defaults. Subprocess overrides affect only the child. Python calls temporarily change the current process's environment, working directory, and output streams; use separate processes for parallel Python calculations. Environment settings must be applied before the relevant native library initializes.

None scratch_dir StrOrPath | None

The calculation directory, not its parent; not accepted with a list of inputs. If None, create a directory in the system's temporary directory. Each concurrent call needs its own directory. This directory, including any existing contents, is deleted when rm_scratch_dir is True.

None rm_scratch_dir bool

Delete the calculation directory after execution, decoding, and file collection finish, including on failure.

True collect_logs bool

Retain merged stdout/stderr in ProgramOutput.logs. Available logs are always retained for failed calculations.

True collect_files bool

Collect files from the calculation directory, excluding files supplied in input_data.files. FileInput always collects these files. Decoders can access generated files regardless of this setting.

False collect_wfn bool

Collect wavefunction files identified by the codec. Not every codec supports this. Ignored when collect_files is True, which retains all generated files including wavefunction files.

False update_func Callable[..., None] | None

Callback accepting (all_logs, new_logs), both strings. Subprocess updates arrive during execution; Python output is delivered after invocation. No callback is made for empty output. For a list of inputs it receives (index, all_logs, new_logs), where index is the input's position, and is called from the threads running the calculations, so it must be thread-safe.

None update_interval float | None

Minimum seconds between subprocess log updates; defaults to 0.5. Updates are line-based, and final output is delivered without waiting for this interval. Has no effect on Python calls.

None print_logs bool

Print merged stdout/stderr using the update callback. Ignored when update_func is supplied. Python logs print after invocation. For a list, each line is prefixed with its input's index, e.g. [3].

False raise_exc bool

Raise a qccompute exception on calculation failure, with the completed ProgramOutput attached as .prog_output. If False, return the failed output instead. Partial results and diagnostics are retained when available. For a list, every calculation runs first; then ComputeErrors (an ExceptionGroup) is raised if any failed, holding each failure's exception and every output in .outputs.

True propagate_wfn bool

For integrations that request child calculations, such as geometry optimization, use the child codec's restart support to prepare each input from the previous result. Requires a child-calculation integration and support for collecting and restarting from wavefunctions.

False options Mapping[str, Any] | None

Program-specific decode options passed to the codec, such as {"collect_rotamers": True} for CREST. Each codec declares the options it accepts in codec.options; unknown keys are rejected.

None timeout float | None

Seconds each external program may run before it and the processes it started are killed, raising ProgramTimeoutError with any partial results attached. Applies to every subprocess, including child calculations of Python integrations such as geomeTRIC; a Python callable itself is not interrupted.

None executables Mapping[str, str] | None

Executables to run, keyed by program name, such as {"orca": "/opt/orca/orca"}. Child calculations of Python integrations such as geomeTRIC use the same mapping; entries for programs that do not run are ignored. Without an entry, the environment variable QCCOMPUTE_<PROGRAM>_EXECUTABLE (for example QCCOMPUTE_ORCA_EXECUTABLE) is used, and otherwise the program is found on PATH. Bare names are looked up on PATH; the program always runs by its absolute path, recorded in execution.extras["executable"].

None max_workers int | None

For a list of inputs, the CPU threads program calculations may use at once. Defaults to the number of CPU cores this process may use. Each calculation counts the threads its codec declares (ORCA pal, Psi4 -n, CREST threads; one otherwise), and each GPU calculation gets its own devices through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Ignored for a single input.

None

Returns:

Type Description ProgramOutput[InputType, Data] | list[ProgramOutput[InputType, Data]]

A ProgramOutput containing scientific results, execution metadata, and the

ProgramOutput[InputType, Data] | list[ProgramOutput[InputType, Data]]

requested logs and files, or a list of them in input order for a list of

ProgramOutput[InputType, Data] | list[ProgramOutput[InputType, Data]]

inputs. Failed calculations may contain partial results.

Raises:

Type Description CodecNotFoundError

No codec is available for the requested program.

InputError

Inputs or compute options are unsupported or invalid.

ProgramNotFoundError

The executable cannot be found, or a codec explicitly reports an unavailable dependency.

ProgramTimeoutError

A program exceeded timeout.

ExternalProgramError

Execution, decoding, artifact collection, or cleanup fails. Unexpected codec exceptions also use this category.

ComputeErrors

For a list of inputs, some calculations failed.

Calculation exceptions are raised only when raise_exc is True.

Source code in src/qccompute/main.py 
def compute(
    input_data: InputType | Sequence[InputType],
    *,
    codec: qccodec.Codec | None = None,
    environment: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    scratch_dir: StrOrPath | None = None,
    rm_scratch_dir: bool = True,
    collect_logs: bool = True,
    collect_files: bool = False,
    collect_wfn: bool = False,
    update_func: Callable[..., None] | None = None,
    update_interval: float | None = None,
    print_logs: bool = False,
    raise_exc: bool = True,
    propagate_wfn: bool = False,
    options: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    timeout: float | None = None,
    executables: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    max_workers: int | None = None,
) -> ProgramOutput[InputType, Data] | list[ProgramOutput[InputType, Data]]:
    """Compute one input, or a list of inputs in parallel, with a local runner.

    A single input returns a single ``ProgramOutput``. A list (or tuple) returns a
    list of outputs in input order; its inputs may be for different programs, and
    every other argument applies to each of them. Calculations that run as programs
    (ORCA, xtb, Psi4, ...) run side by side in threads. Calculations that run in
    Python (geomeTRIC, tblite) take over a process's output streams while they run,
    so two or more of them run side by side in worker processes, which start with the
    numerical libraries' thread counts set to their share. All of them draw on the
    ``max_workers`` budget. Inputs a codec can evaluate together (machine-learned
    potentials sharing a model) run in batches in this process, one call per batch
    of up to ``codec.max_batch``; ``execution.extras`` records ``batch_size`` and
    ``batch_index``.

    Args:
        input_data: A qcdata input object, such as ProgramInput or FileInput, or a
            list of them.
        codec: The ``qccodec.Codec`` translating this program's inputs and outputs.
            If None, resolve one with ``qccodec.get_codec(input_data)``: a codec
            registered with ``qccodec.register``, a built-in, or one installed by
            another package.
        environment: Process environment overrides mapping strings to strings.
            Applied after the inherited environment and codec defaults. Subprocess
            overrides affect only the child. Python calls temporarily change the
            current process's environment, working directory, and output streams;
            use separate processes for parallel Python calculations. Environment
            settings must be applied before the relevant native library initializes.
        scratch_dir: The calculation directory, not its parent; not accepted with a
            list of inputs. If None, create a
            directory in the system's temporary directory. Each concurrent call
            needs its own directory. This directory, including any existing
            contents, is deleted when rm_scratch_dir is True.
        rm_scratch_dir: Delete the calculation directory after execution, decoding,
            and file collection finish, including on failure.
        collect_logs: Retain merged stdout/stderr in ProgramOutput.logs. Available
            logs are always retained for failed calculations.
        collect_files: Collect files from the calculation directory, excluding files
            supplied in input_data.files. FileInput always collects these files.
            Decoders can access generated files regardless of this setting.
        collect_wfn: Collect wavefunction files identified by the codec. Not every
            codec supports this. Ignored when collect_files is True, which retains
            all generated files including wavefunction files.
        update_func: Callback accepting (all_logs, new_logs), both strings.
            Subprocess updates arrive during execution; Python output is delivered
            after invocation. No callback is made for empty output. For a list of
            inputs it receives (index, all_logs, new_logs), where index is the
            input's position, and is called from the threads running the
            calculations, so it must be thread-safe.
        update_interval: Minimum seconds between subprocess log updates; defaults
            to 0.5. Updates are line-based, and final output is delivered without
            waiting for this interval. Has no effect on Python calls.
        print_logs: Print merged stdout/stderr using the update callback. Ignored
            when update_func is supplied. Python logs print after invocation. For a
            list, each line is prefixed with its input's index, e.g. ``[3]``.
        raise_exc: Raise a qccompute exception on calculation failure, with the
            completed ProgramOutput attached as .prog_output. If False, return
            the failed output instead. Partial results and diagnostics are retained
            when available. For a list, every calculation runs first; then
            ``ComputeErrors`` (an ``ExceptionGroup``) is raised if any failed, holding
            each failure's exception and every output in ``.outputs``.
        propagate_wfn: For integrations that request child calculations, such as
            geometry optimization, use the child codec's restart support to prepare
            each input from the previous result. Requires a child-calculation
            integration and support for collecting and restarting from wavefunctions.
        options: Program-specific decode options passed to the codec, such as
            ``{"collect_rotamers": True}`` for CREST. Each codec declares the
            options it accepts in ``codec.options``; unknown keys are rejected.
        timeout: Seconds each external program may run before it and the processes
            it started are killed, raising ``ProgramTimeoutError`` with any partial
            results attached. Applies to every subprocess, including child
            calculations of Python integrations such as geomeTRIC; a Python
            callable itself is not interrupted.
        executables: Executables to run, keyed by program name, such as
            ``{"orca": "/opt/orca/orca"}``. Child calculations of Python
            integrations such as geomeTRIC use the same mapping; entries for programs
            that do not run are ignored. Without an entry, the environment variable
            ``QCCOMPUTE_<PROGRAM>_EXECUTABLE`` (for example
            ``QCCOMPUTE_ORCA_EXECUTABLE``) is used, and otherwise the program is
            found on ``PATH``. Bare names are looked up on ``PATH``; the program
            always runs by its absolute path, recorded in
            ``execution.extras["executable"]``.
        max_workers: For a list of inputs, the CPU threads program calculations may
            use at once. Defaults to the number of CPU cores this process may use.
            Each calculation counts the threads its codec declares (ORCA ``pal``,
            Psi4 ``-n``, CREST ``threads``; one otherwise), and each GPU calculation
            gets its own devices through ``CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES``. Ignored for a
            single input.

    Returns:
        A ProgramOutput containing scientific results, execution metadata, and the
        requested logs and files, or a list of them in input order for a list of
        inputs. Failed calculations may contain partial results.

    Raises:
        CodecNotFoundError: No codec is available for the requested program.
        InputError: Inputs or compute options are unsupported or invalid.
        ProgramNotFoundError: The executable cannot be found, or a codec explicitly
            reports an unavailable dependency.
        ProgramTimeoutError: A program exceeded ``timeout``.
        ExternalProgramError: Execution, decoding, artifact collection, or cleanup
            fails. Unexpected codec exceptions also use this category.

        ComputeErrors: For a list of inputs, some calculations failed.

    Calculation exceptions are raised only when raise_exc is True.
    """
    if isinstance(input_data, Sequence) and not isinstance(input_data, str | bytes):
        return compute_list(
            _compute_one,
            input_data,
            compute_batch=_compute_batch,
            max_workers=max_workers,
            raise_exc=raise_exc,
            update_func=update_func,
            print_logs=print_logs,
            options={
                "codec": codec,
                "environment": environment,
                "scratch_dir": scratch_dir,
                "rm_scratch_dir": rm_scratch_dir,
                "collect_logs": collect_logs,
                "collect_files": collect_files,
                "collect_wfn": collect_wfn,
                "update_interval": update_interval,
                "propagate_wfn": propagate_wfn,
                "options": options,
                "timeout": timeout,
                "executables": executables,
            },
        )
    return _compute_one(
        input_data,
        codec=codec,
        environment=environment,
        scratch_dir=scratch_dir,
        rm_scratch_dir=rm_scratch_dir,
        collect_logs=collect_logs,
        collect_files=collect_files,
        collect_wfn=collect_wfn,
        update_func=update_func,
        update_interval=update_interval,
        print_logs=print_logs,
        raise_exc=raise_exc,
        propagate_wfn=propagate_wfn,
        options=options,
        timeout=timeout,
        executables=executables,
    )

docs.title: Examples for each program
docs.text: Complete, runnable scripts for every program and calculation type, with every common option shown and the program's quirks explained, are on the qccodec program pages. The examples here cover qccompute itself: running a program from your own input files and defining a codec for a program qccodec doesn't support.

docs.title: Programs
docs.text:
qccompute runs programs; everything specific to a program lives in its qccodec codec. The qccodec documentation has a page for each supported program, explaining how a ProgramInput maps onto it (keywords, solvent, parallelism, quirks), with a complete, runnable example script for every calculation type:

  • CREST
  • geomeTRIC
  • ORCA
  • Psi4
  • TeraChem and its servers
  • xtb

Program-specific decode options are passed as compute(input_data, options={...}); each codec declares what it accepts in codec.options. A program not on PATH, or shadowed by another command of the same name, is selected with compute(..., executables={"orca": "/path/to/orca"}) or the environment variable QCCOMPUTE_<PROGRAM>_EXECUTABLE.

Programs qccodec doesn't support yet can be run by writing a codec in your own script; see Custom codec.
